title: Old Fortran, silent error
why: Legacy modernisation was real work. The bug here is a classic one: implicit typing.
rubric: Finds that N and I are implicitly INTEGER while SUM is implicitly REAL
Recognises the integer division in forming the mean
Names IMPLICIT NONE as the remedy
prompt:
This Fortran 77 code is meant to compute a mean, but for X = [1.0, 2.0] it returns 1.0 instead of 1.5. Why?

      SUBROUTINE MEAN(X, N, RES)
      REAL X(N), RES
      SUM = 0.0
      DO 10 I = 1, N
         SUM = SUM + X(I)
   10 CONTINUE
      RES = SUM / N
      RETURN
      END
